body: NPC work split: FSM/steering inline for all NPCs every tick, perception time-sliced (4 slots), spawning throttled (spawns_per_tick); nothing on AsyncComputeTaskPool. Rejected: async perception/spawn tasks - probe shows 64 Tnua NPC cost ~0.2 ms/tick over a 0.56 ms city baseline and 0.6 us per LOS ray, so a task round-trip would add a tick of latency for no gain.

Spawn civilians at random points on sidewalk-graph EDGES inside the 60-120 m ring, not on nodes. Rejected: node spawn (GDD 6.1 wording) - seed 1 has 579 nodes/1134 edges with edges >= 4.5 m and only 35 edges (1604 m) in the ring; nodes are too few and two spawns on one node overlap capsules.

Corpse = TnuaToggle::Disabled + RigidBody::Static + CollisionLayers::NONE on death. Rejected: keep Tnua with zero motion like dummies (an invisible standing capsule blocks walkers and bullets) and removing TnuaController (leaves Tnua sensor entities, more archetype churn). Probe: corpse moved 0.00000 m over 128 ticks, chest ray passes, a walker walks through.

In-frame test via a sim resource ViewCone {origin, forward, half_angle} written by the client camera (diagonal bounding cone of the frustum). Rejected: AimIntent + a FOV copy in population.ron (two owners of the FOV, breaks one-source-per-value).

Civilian look = per-entity tint of the one shipped model. Rejected for T8: other Kenney GLBs as civilian models - bevy_gltf 0.19.1 AnimationTargetId path starts with the glTF root node name (character-male-a vs character-female-b), so the shared graph's clips would not drive them.

NPC AI set runs in GameState::Playing OR Wasted. Rejected: PlayingSystems - during Wasted drive_characters keeps consuming the last MoveIntent, so frozen AI would walk NPCs straight off the graph for 4.5 s.
No separation steering and no stuck detector in T8: Tnua capsules already push apart. Rejected: grid-based separation (extra O(N) pass + data) until QA/owner shows a reproducible stuck crowd.

Rejected PLAN_V2 step 8 'publish an initial view in PreUpdate after Loading->Playing spawned the player, before the first fixed tick': bevy_app-0.19.1 main_schedule.rs orders First, PreUpdate, StateTransition, RunFixedMainLoop, so the OnTransition player spawn happens after PreUpdate in the same frame. The view stays None until follow_player+publish in PostUpdate; initial fill runs on the first fixed tick with a valid view (one frame later).

Spawn on sidewalk graph NODES (GDD 6.1 literal), one civilian per node (4 m separation < 4.5 m min node spacing), shuffled eligible-node list instead of random attempts. Alternative rejected: PLAN.md edge points. Measured seed 1 at player spawn: 16 nodes in 60-120 m, 24 in 20-120 m (18 outside a 120 deg cone); cap 40 is reached over seconds as walkers vacate nodes, not at load.

Q1 gate uses real GLB loading in a headless client test (GltfPlugin+WorldSerializationPlugin+AnimationPlugin+ImagePlugin+MeshPlugin, no render) and asserts leg-left joint rotation changes per model. Alternative rejected: structure-only graph assertions. Probe: own clips rotate leg 1.183 rad, male-a clips on female-b 0.0000 rad.

Test binaries failed with 'could not find civilian in gta_sim' although the lib built: the parallel worktree .worktrees/showcase shares target/ and its gta_sim rlib has the same metadata hash (workspace-relative path hash), so cargo treated the other tree's rlib as fresh. Workaround: touch crates/gta_sim/src/lib.rs before every cargo command.

Walkers steer to node(to) shifted keep_right=0.5 m right of travel (navigation.ron) instead of node(to) itself. Reason: wander_stays_on_the_graph caught two opposing walkers on one edge colliding head-on (0.6 m apart) and one ending 1.58 m off the line (> 1.5 m sidewalk half-width). Alternative rejected: widening the gate tolerance (hides the defect) or separation steering (extra O(N) pass).
Corpse self-interrupt fixed in perceive (callers are not offered corpses) instead of the review's FSM-side filter: nearest-threat selection would let a nearer body mask a new gunshot (flip b RED).

Reading CameraView over BRP with tools/qa/brp.py Game.resource() fails: it casts the value to int, so only scalar resources work. Used game.call('world.get_resources', {resource: game.resource_path(..)}) directly.
